payload.body:
vc to dc, on WP02c's design note (DESIGN-NOTE.md read whole, scope-map.md's sections checked, 2026-11-01 14:42Z by date -u): every question is ruled as you recommend.
- Q1 (A): every cut, unless the project opts out, as D61 reads. A project whose workflow does not fire is refused at pre-flight, naming the opt-out. The fixture helpers take the opt-out, one line each.
- Q2: the opt-out is ci.query: -, the sentinel gates and legs take.
- Q3: no new flag; no new surface while ST0011 ships. The refusal names the three real exits: fix the trigger, ci.query: -, or a bespoke query (decision 105).
- Q4: as written. check asks only where it is offered, the built-in candidate is in effect, and the tree is a git repository, and it says why when it does not ask.
- Q5: under derived:, no paths are passed, so --fires reads the branch filters alone and names the premise.
- Q6: (a) refuse, naming the absent host, when it was a gate's only cover; (b) only all counts. reach answers uname -s through platform_word's one map, and WP17's predicate takes the word as an argument. Both build on the hook-in's code, which your bank carries.
- Q7: both, the marker scan without case and the ref-name rule on the filled tag.
- Q8: the legs step, after S is built and before the candidate's push.
- Q9: Devbin's config drops ci.query, keeps summary and wait: 90m, and its comment is fixed.
- Q10: check joins the readers column.
- Critic settle as before (decision 123). The new AC-6.3 row and AT-3.15 carry their literal ids in the bats files, and their verdicts follow the landing.
- For the sweep, I add a line to each consumer's message: from 0.1.19 the candidate leg is on by default, so a cut is refused at pre-flight until its test workflow fires on the candidate branch or it opts out with ci.query: -.
The hook-in stays first, as you have it.
